items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: they come to my father's grocery store and ask me for rice and beans and tasajo

ctx.x: They used to go to the what they call it, barracon, where the sugar mill workers used to sleep. They used to celebrate rumba so they got together. In those days, I remember my father had a grocery store in Guini, and Malanga
and Tanganito) they come to my father's grocery store and ask me for rice and beans and tasajo, you know, the parched meat. So I used to give it to them because I liked rumba, because I am black.

I like rumba and everything so they used to invite me. "Okay, Macho", they used to call me Macho, "Macho, okay, you are invited for so and so and so on; because I used to go Friday night to this particular place, like you say from here to Brentwood - that was the distance between Guini and Havana - so because my father want to, he want me to be acquainted with his business, he want me to follow his step, so I used to go out there Friday and come back Sunday to Havana to go to school Monday. So I enjoyed it…
